title: OKRs + Mini Experiments Sprintboard (personal scratchpad)
content:
Context:
Quick personal scratchpad for Q1-ish OKRs + a couple of 2-week experiments I want to run in the next sprint window. This lives here as my working draft — share selectively. Notes are short, sometimes half-formed, and include ad-hoc metric checks (I paste queries), hypotheses, and immediate next-actions for the week.

Objective draft (O1): Reduce developer friction for onboarding to the Redwood Console SDK by improving first-10-minute success rate
KR1: Increase "first-10-minute" success (successful hello-world request + correct auth) from 62% -> 80% for new signups during trial.
KR2: Reduce median time-to-first-success (TTFS) from 10.2m -> 6.0m measured over developer sandbox traffic.
KR3: Ship 3 guided quickstarts (node, python, terraform) and get >= 100 unique completions each in preview.

Objective draft (O2): Improve signal quality for rollout experiments so rollouts can confidently rely on automated metrics
KR1: Get baseline false positive rate of rollout regressions under 5% across 10 pilot prompt sets.
KR2: Standardize 1 inference-quality metric pipeline (token-level perplexity + semantic-similarity A/B) for every canary.

Mini-experiments (2-week boxes):
- Experiment A: "Onboarding nudges" (week 1-2)
  Hypothesis: sending an in-console checklist overlay with 3 steps increases first-10-minute success and TTFS.
  Variant A: checklist + inline code sample. Variant B: checklist + auto-open `curl` example for hosted API.
  Metrics: success rate, TTFS, help center click-through, support tickets opened.
  Quick metrics check (BigQuery):
    SELECT
      COUNTIF(event='first_success') / COUNT(*) as success_rate,
      APPROX_QUANTILES(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(success_time, signup_time, SECOND), 100)[OFFSET(50)] as median_ttfs
    FROM `redwood-prod.analytics.onboarding_events`
    WHERE signup_date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE();
  Launch checklist: feature flag (ff-onboard-checklist), experiment id, slack ping #devex, add to /experiments board.

- Experiment B: "Lightweight eval checkpoint" (week 1-2)
  Hypothesis: adding a small semantic-similarity threshold test during rollout reduces regressions without hurting SLOs.
  Implementation: run 50 sample prompts through new model variant; compute mean cosine(sim_ref, output_emb) using embedding endpoint; block if mean < 0.78.
  Note: need support from infra to run at canary scale. Ticket: INF-4123 (linked).

Weekly check-ins (scratch):
- 2025-03-03 (mon): set feature flag for Experiment A in dev. Talked with Jin about telemetry schema. He suggested tracking `help_click_reason` as a string enum — do it.
- 2025-03-05 (wed): small spike revealed `signup_time` missing for ~4% of sandboxes (edge cases: github-oauth piped signups). Create data-cleaning piece.
- 2025-03-06 (thu): ran manual similarity baseline for 100 samples, mean cosine=0.81. Good signal but noisy on longer responses.

Retro fragments (post-sprint):
- What went well: quick flag rollout, low deployment friction.
- Pain points: flaky telemetry, ambiguous error states for first-success. Need stricter schema and backfill.
- Learnings: tiny checks (50 samples) can catch gross regressions but we need per-prompt stability tracking (signal drift).

Open questions / discussion items for 1:1 with manager:
- Acceptable tradeoff between blocking canary on similarity vs. allowing manual overrides (who owns override? SRE or product?).
- Priority of data-cleaning vs. adding new quickstarts (both useful but limited cycles this sprint).
- Do we formalize a "first-10-minute" definition across teams or keep as product-specific metric?

Action items (next 7 days):
1) Finalize experiment variants and push flag for variant A only in dev (owner: me) — target EOD 2025-03-07.
2) Create data-cleaning ticket for missing signup_time and assign to Maya (link draft in ticket body).
3) Draft short README for guided quickstarts (skeleton in /docs/quickstarts) and assign PR (owner: Jin).
4) Add a small smoke-run in CI that computes the 50-sample similarity baseline during canary runs (coordinate with infra).

Notes to self (messy):
- Be explicit in README about API key scopes so new devs don't get 403s midway.
- Consider a short inline video (60s) for the python quickstart if completions < 60 after 2 weeks.
- Slack copy for onboarding nudge: "Welcome! 3 small steps to make your first request work — try Node example, check API key, run sample." Keep friendly.

Measurement sources & ownership:
- TTFS & first-success events: analytics -> infra-telemetry (contact: Maya Patel).
- Embedding similarity computation: evals service -> Jin Park (PR #824).
- Quickstart completions: console frontend metrics (component: quickstarts).

Quick wins I can do this week (no approvals):
- Tighten help copy on Node quickstart in Console (5–10m).
- Add debug logging around signup_time for sandbox flows (create tiny PR).

If this still smells like scope creep: split into "data hygiene" (high priority) and "growth experiment" (medium). Triage in sync with manager.

End-of-note: save this as working copy. Will prune and publish a cleaned version to Confluence if manager wants to share more widely.
